Content:
I feel like there were a lot of times through the video where you really push that something is unprecedented or never happened before in world history, and like I mean no shit in the nicest way possible lol. International anything is unprecedented because it's basically only the last century and a half that humans have been able to have international conflicts, or things that lead to them. Go figure that now us humans trying to uphold international law generally for the first time obviously isn't going to go swimmingly.

I feel like all this sorta language does is drive engagement because it sensationalizes the information you're giving out. Which while all these things are reprehensible, you can't just skip over how new all this is and the realization that all laws are just an imaginary thing to help hold power and authority. It works fine with law enforcement within governments because the government holds ultimate power over the people, but on the international level you're just banking on the support of other nations who themselves have situations they need to handle. Like Mongolia, I feel like them being fully bordered fully justifies them welcoming Putin rather than arresting him because it could literally destroy them: saying that "helps set a precedent" feels wrong when it's literally about their survival as a nation. Similar situations with the other leaders who either weren't a part of the ICC or never followed the ICC to begin with, making them sorta rogue ICC state who should be kicked out.

Regardless of all this, all this video makes me think is that we need a massive worldwide civilian and government uprising against these kinds of leaders and take direct action against them. This would undoubtably be a World War and it would be a very bloody and costly war. My biggest reason to not have this is that global no institutions nor governments can be trusted enough to do such a task even together in a way that would actually benefit mankind. The only reason to go through with a such a global conflict would be for power: even if that power is viewed as a good thing to get rid of these horrible leaders who make countless suffer, it's too much power for any group to hold effectively without corruption. It'd be committing the exact crimes it's fighting to stop, hypocritical from its onset yet one of the few things that I can think would even be effective in the long term against these sorts of atrocities.

As it stands, the fact that an international court even exists and that it's making these attempts is at least a very good sign for things to come compared to basically all of human history up until this point. Yes, things in the last few decades have gotten more violent and global tensions have not been higher since the 1930s, but in the very long term humans are and will always be on an overall upward path towards better peace. Not that there will be true world peace, but that we will get to a point were things like these very very rarely ever happen; like the resurgence of a cured disease, specific ideas and events can cause an outbreak, but it will be managed and fixed if not stopped before it happens.
